stem: A relation from $X=\{-1, 1, 2\}$ to $Y=\{2, 4, 6\}$ is made of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ with $a \in X$ first and $b \in Y$ second. Tap every ordered pair that could belong to a relation from $X$ to $Y$ (all of $X \times Y$).
solution: A relation from X to Y is written with ordered pairs (a, b): the first member a comes from X and the second member b from Y.
Pair each member of X with every member of Y: with -1 we get (-1, 2), (-1, 4), (-1, 6).
These 9 pairs form X × Y; any relation from X to Y, such as the pairs where b = 2a + 4, is chosen from among them.
notes: Honest limit: this widget builds the whole of X × Y, the pool every relation from X to Y draws from. It does not choose the pairs that satisfy a rule, so it covers only the pair-order part of lo:u1-2-1 and not the rule-based pairs of the anchor. missing-pairs is not mapped. lo:u1-2-1 has only the pair-order misconception, and an incomplete list is a different error that would mean a different misconception. It is not mapped to pair-order-reversed. extra-pairs cannot be emitted for this spec.
